rationale.wallClock: Stall guard. A render that hangs is killed at maxDurationSeconds, so the wall ceiling bounds how long one job may occupy the render slot. Unchanged by this contract.
rationale.cpu: Device-load guard. CPU seconds are summed over the whole browser process tree, so a render occupying N cores accrues them N times faster than wall clock. maxCpuSeconds is therefore a different quantity from maxDurationSeconds and must not share its ceiling.
rationale.parallelism: cpuParallelismMaximum is the highest average core occupancy one render may declare for its wall budget. At 8 the guard stays reachable on the 16-core acceptance hosts (half of what the machine could physically deliver), so genuine runaway fan-out still trips it, while a legitimate multi-core composition render (measured at roughly 2-3 cores average) has room.
rationale.tightening: Sharing the 300 second wall ceiling left the CPU guard inert on short budgets: a 1 second wall budget could declare 300 CPU seconds, a figure no host can reach inside 1 wall second. The derived ceiling rejects that and every wall budget below 37.5 seconds is now bounded more tightly than before.
